subject: Re: Design review - attested proxy & local keybroker sync for VPC private deployments
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: IT-Sec <it-sec@acmecorp.com>, Acme Infra <infra@acmeops.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Key sync for private deploy - initial ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're evaluating Redwood Private for our on-prem inference cluster and need to validate the KMS/HSM integration surface. Two points we want to confirm before architecture review: 

1) We cannot have persistent plaintext keys leaving our vaults. Any sync must be encrypted with an attested handshake and only transport wrapped keys or ephemeral KEKs.
2) Our ops require the ability to rotate application-level wrapping keys without downtime (short TTLs preferred).

Could you circulate a design proposal that covers: attestation model for the proxy, transport-layer encryption for key sync, and an operational rotation playbook (including offline disaster recovery)? Added Hannah and Marcus from Redwood to help.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Security Lead, Acme Corp

Attachments: request-form-acme.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key sync for private deploy - initial ask

Olivia,

Appreciate the clear requirements. Attached is a compact design summary and sequence diagram (see attachments). High-level proposal:

- Attested proxy: a small customer-owned VM in the VPC that runs our attestation agent. It performs remote attestation to the Redwood control plane using mutually authenticated mTLS + TPM quote verification. The proxy never exports unwrapped customer key material; it accepts wrapped key blobs and stores them in the local HSM/KMS.

- Transport model: all key exchange occurs in two layers: 1) connection layer (mTLS with certs pinned to the attestation result), 2) payload layer (a per-sync ephemeral KEK established via ECDH inside the attested session). Customer HSM signs an attestation claim; Redwood returns an ephemeral wrapping material which is used once.

- Rotation/TTL: we propose a lease-based model where application wrapping keys are short-lived (default 6 hours) and backed by an auto-renewing KEK envelope. Rotations are staged: preview, staged rotate (dual-write), cutover, and revoke. Dual-write means both old and new envelopes accepted for a 15 minute window to avoid downtime.

- DR/offline: for fully air-gapped recoveries, we support a sealed-envelope export using split quorum (Shamir) into operator-controlled fragments. These fragments are retained by customer custodians and Redwood support only holds metadata and notarized attestations.

Next steps: I can run a 60-minute architecture review with Acme, propose a canary plan, and produce a runbook for the rotation ceremony. Attached: attested-proxy-draft-diagram.png, key-sync-sequence-v1.pdf

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: attested-proxy-draft-diagram.png (PNG, 220KB); key-sync-sequence-v1.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key sync for private deploy - initial ask

Sofia / Olivia,

A few engineering notes to add to Sofia's plan: 

- We should require cert attestation renewal on change of underlying HSM firmware or operator CA rotation to avoid stale bindings. Automate cert re-issue post-attestation.
- For transport, recommend AEAD (AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305) for payloads; include a replay-protection nonce derived from the attestation quote.
- On the dual-write window: make it configurable per-customer. We'll propose safe defaults but allow Acme to set 0s for forced rollover during maintenance windows.

Also: propose an observability hook that emits only metadata (not key identifiers) into Redwood Console for TTL and renewal metrics. This helps operations without leaking KMS secrets.

Happy to walk through these in the review.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key sync for private deploy - initial ask

Team,

Operational edge-case I want captured in the runbook: what happens when the attested proxy fails mid-rotation and cannot complete dual-write? Proposed guardrails: 

1) Rotation attempt should be idempotent and checkpointed in orchestration metadata. If the proxy loses connectivity, orchestrator retries with exponential backoff and stalls further cutovers.
2) If retries exceed threshold, we auto-revert to the last-known-good envelope and emit a high-priority alert to both Acme ops and Redwood on-call.
3) For emergency manual recovery: provide a signed recovery token flow where Acme operator can produce a hardware-signed token (TPM-backed) that authorizes a one-time emergency unwrap under dual-operator approval. This should be logged and require DocuSign approval for audit trail.

I'll draft the state machine diagrams for the runbook and share by EOD.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key sync for private deploy - initial ask

Olivia — thanks for the prompt. From a compliance perspective this aligns with our requirements for BYOK integrations at the enterprise tier. A couple of small asks before we lock the runbook: 

- Confirm retention windows for the attestation logs (we recommend 2 years for audit, archived to customer-managed S3/GCS).
- Provide an explicit list of allowed operator roles and the approval chain for emergency recoveries (we'll need to map to Acme's RBAC).
- For split-quorum sealed exports, confirm the minimum shard threshold and storage guardrails (we recommend 3-of-5 default).

If Acme can confirm those items, we'll finalize the architecture doc, schedule a 60-minute review for next week, and produce the rotation ceremony checklist.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
